title.narrative: Activity under preparation Support to Green TVET and E-learning in Bangladesh

description.narrative: Bangladesh has made strong progress on economic growth and poverty reduction but continues to face structural challenges in creating productive jobs, increasing labour productivity, and addressing high climate vulnerability. The country is entering a critical window where demographic pressure, green transition commitments and digital transformation converge. Each year, around two million young people enter the labour market, while investments in renewable energy, infrastructure and digital systems are accelerating. Without a rapid transformation of the skills system, there is a significant risk of rising youth underemployment and missed economic opportunities.This action responds to this strategic challenge by positioning Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) not as a standalone education intervention, but as a key enabler of Bangladesh¿s economic transformation. While TVET is recognised in Bangladesh as a key policy instrument, important gaps remain in curriculum relevance, instructor capacity, industry linkages, e-learning systems and equitable access. Building on previous EU support, notably the Human Capital Development Programme (HCDP 21), the action supports the Government of Bangladesh in implementing key policy frameworks, including the TVET Implementation Plan 2025¿2030, the National Education Policy, the National Skills Development Policy, and the E-learning Action Plan. The European Union brings distinct added value by combining policy dialogue, budget support, and investments under the Global Gateway strategy, including in renewable energy and sustainable infrastructure, linking skills development directly to green and digital transitions. Unlike other partners focusing primarily on project-based interventions, the EU intervention targets system-level transformation, linking policy reform, financing and labour market outcomes.The action has two specific objectives: 1) Improve employability of jobseekers and graduating from the TVET system, particularly in the priority green sectors. 2) Improve quality, inclusiveness and effectiveness of TVET delivery through increased application of green competency-based and blended learning teaching practices.These efforts will improve labour market alignment, expand access to flexible training, and strengthen institutional capacity. The action is aligned with the EU Multi-annual Indicative Programme (MIP) 2021¿2027 and supports the Global Gateway strategy by linking skills development with green and digital transitions. It contributes primarily to SDG 4 (Quality Education), while also supporting SDG 5 (Gender Equality), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities), and SDG 13 (Climate Action).The action will be implemented through a EUR 48 million package, including EUR 44 million in budget support and EUR 4 million in complementary technical assistance. The EUR 48 million targets system-level reform across a TVET system serving millions of learners, making it highly cost-effective compared to fragmented project-based interventions. The budget support modality will reinforce policy dialogue, incentivise reform implementation through performance-based disbursement, and support alignment between policy priorities and public expenditure. By leveraging government systems and aligning with national policy frameworks, the action ensures scalability and sustainability beyond the duration of EU support. It complements ongoing support from development partners, including GIZ, the World Bank, ADB and ILO, and contributes to coordinated sector dialogue
